memory_lessons.applicability: Use the prior result as a whole-call reference, not evidence that the atomic path itself caused the observed speed or that it beats a matched control.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior T3 program was valid and measured 6.492 µs over three samples; the baseline measured 47.079 µs over three samples. The catalog contains one distinct T3 program and no alternative, so these measurements do not isolate atomic, memset, or tile-size effects.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure repeated whole-call timings for the memset-plus-atomic and same-tile two-kernel control paths, and retain the per-size results if the controller reports them.

proposal.hypothesis: The sole observed T3 program was correct and measured 6.49 µs on average versus the baseline's 47.08 µs, but the catalog has only one distinct T3 program and provides no matched atomic-versus-control result. This contrasting candidate tests a warp-level CTA reduction with 256-, 1024-, and 4096-element tiles. The atomic path includes default-stream memset plus one atomicAdd per CTA; the non-atomic path uses the same 1024-element first-pass mapping and a second finalization kernel. The broad size dispatch is for whole-call comparison, not a prediction that atomics win.

retained: Kept the original 128-thread multi-pass reducer for n < 4096 and added explicit handling for nonpositive n and n == 1.
Added a 256-thread CTA reduction using warp-level reduction and shared storage for one partial per warp, replacing per-level CTA-wide synchronization in the tiled path.
Added 256-, 1024-, and 4096-element CTA tile configurations; each CTA contributes one sum through atomicAdd in the atomic path.

Added a default-stream output memset before the atomic kernel and a non-atomic two-kernel control that uses the same 1024-element first-pass mapping, overwrites all partials, and finalizes them without an extra allocation.
